rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai observes that scripture is actively attributed to God in contexts of praise, while passive 'were given' appears in rebuke; 2:144 condemns those who know the truth yet evade it.
rows.anchor: إذا كان المقام مقامَ مدح وثناء، أظهر ذاته ونسب إيتاء الكتاب إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He extends the agency pattern to inheritance of scripture: God names himself as giver in praise, but passive inheritance or carrying is used in condemnatory contexts; good is attributed to God and evil is veiled.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أن الله سبحانه يذكر ذاته في الخير العام وينسبه إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the al-Aʿrāf account, the passive 'it was said' suppresses explicit mention of God because the people do not merit that honor, like the passive 'were given the Book' wording.
rows.anchor: فبنى القول للمجهول في الأعراف ولم يظهر الرب نفسه لأنهم هنا لا يستحقون هذا التشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:58 the fa makes eating follow entry immediately; in 7:161 the waw links eating with settling, which follows entry and leaves its timing open, so the provision in al-Baqara is more generous.
rows.anchor: أن الأكل في الأولى بعد الدخول، وفي الثانية مع السكن، فقال في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of 'abundantly' in al-Baqara suits its enumeration of blessings and honor, whereas both al-Aʿrāf stories omit it amid punishment and reproach; this parallels Moses and Adam.
rows.anchor: لأنه مناسب لتعداد النعم ولم يقل: (رغداً) في سورة الأعراف لأن المقام تقريع وتأنيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In paradise 'abundantly' precedes 'wherever you wish', while in the world it follows: earthly abundance is limited, and the order avoids equating it with paradise while making heavenly abundance the higher aim.
rows.anchor: كما أن فيه إشارة أن رغد الجنة مقدم على رغد الدنيا، فليعمل العاملون لنيل ذلك الرغد أولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara places prostration before the word of repentance because prostration is nobler and follows the preceding prayer and bowing passage, including 2:44; al-Aʿrāf omits that sequence and delays prostration.
rows.anchor: لأن السجود أشرف من القول لأنه أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara uses the intensive plural khaṭāyā for many sins, fitting its blessing and honoring tone; al-Aʿrāf uses the sound plural khaṭīʾāt, which he says conveys few and suits reproach.
rows.anchor: بجمع الكثرة لأن الخطايا جمع كثرة، وهو مناسب لمقام تعداد النعم والتكريم

words: عَسَىٰ رَبِّي أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ
عَسَىٰ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَٰذَا رَشَدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas retains the speaker's yāʾ in yahdīnī because Moses flees Pharaoh in fear and turns wholly to God; Kahf's less urgent prayer omits it, using the kasra instead.
rows.anchor: الخوف يستدعي أن يلصق الإنسان بمن يحميه ويلقي بنفسه كلها عليه

words: عَسَىٰ رَبِّي أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ
عَسَىٰ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَٰذَا رَشَدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qasas, 'Lord' precedes the guidance verb because the fearful speaker first seeks his protector; Kahf foregrounds guidance because its context asks for right direction amid differing views.
rows.anchor: قدم (الرب) على فعل الهداية لأنه هو الملجأ فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ pronoun occurs more often in Qasas, and guidance is mentioned twelve times there against five in Kahf; the greater recurrence supports the fuller form in Qasas.
rows.anchor: ثم لننظر من ناحية أخرى فإن ياء الضمير تكرر في (القصص) أكثر مما في الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas tells Moses' story at length, while the Kahf prayer occurs briefly within the sleepers' story; Samarrai links the longer account to the longer verb form and the concise account to deletion.
rows.anchor: مقام التبسط والتطويل في (القصص) في قصة موسى أكثر بكثير مما ورد في (الكهف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf retains the yāʾ in al-muhtadī because guidance recurs there seventeen times, more than the combined fourteen in al-Isrāʾ and al-Kahf, where the yāʾ is omitted.
rows.anchor: فقد ورد في الأعراف سبع عشرة مرة، في حين ورد في الإسراء ثماني مرات وفي الكهف ست مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is omitted in Isra's single mention of delaying, but retained in al-Munāfiqūn, where the delaying verb occurs twice; the longer context receives the fuller form.
rows.anchor: تردد فعل التأخير مرتين في سورة (المنافقون) في حين ذكر مرة واحدة في سورة (الإسراء)

words: إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai points to other yāʾ deletions in Kahf, including tarani in 18:39, yuʾtini, tuʿallimni, nabghi, and al-muhtad, as corroborating the omission in yahdin.
rows.anchor: وذلك نحو قوله تعالى: {إِن تَرَنِ أَنَاْ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالاً وَوَلَداً} [الكهف: 39] بحذف الياء من (ترني)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qibla dispute in al-Baqara brought greater fear of people through hostile rumors, so God is explicit in 'fear Me'; al-Māʾida follows Islam's triumph or lacks such hostility, so its yāʾ is omitted.
rows.anchor: فذكر الياء في (اخشوني) في آية البقرة، وحذفها واجتزأ بالكسرة في آيتي المائدة

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ
وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended, repetitive qibla passage runs from the fools' objection and the trial of the change through the command to face Mecca and the Book-holders' refusal; its length suits the explicit pronoun.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه أطال القول ههنا، فكان المناسب أن يطيل بذكر الضيمر أيضاً وهو المناسب لإطالة السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqara's surrounding qibla passage states the divine yāʾ explicitly more often than the other contexts, including 'complete My favor', 'remember Me', and 'thank Me', supporting its explicit yāʾ in 'fear Me'.
rows.anchor: أبرز الضمير (الياء) في سياق آية البقرة أكثر مما في المواطنين الآخرين

words: هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He flags the wording in 6:158 and 7:52–53 as a similar mention-and-omission phenomenon, but says it is not the same type as the preceding yāʾ cases.
rows.anchor: وشبيه بهذا الذكر والحذف وليس منه قوله تعالى
